claims.statement: The Commission states that construction and demolition waste represents more than one third of EU waste and includes high-resource-value components.
The Commission provides guidance for pre-demolition audits and reports wide variation in recycling and recovery across the EU.
The EU Digital Product Passport is designed to expose product information including materials, reuse, and recycling, with construction-product requirements indicated for 2027.

contrary_evidence: Recovery rates vary widely and much construction material is not currently reused at high value.
The DPP construction timeline is indicative and does not itself make a previously installed component acceptable for reuse.

economics.acquisition_route: Property managers, demolition contractors, architects, and insurer or sustainability consultants
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Illustrative, unvalidated path: 50m PLN annual material value at a 15% blended fee could yield 7.5m PLN revenue; at 20% operating margin and 75% founder ownership, a profit-based valuation could plausibly exceed 5m PLN around year 7
economics.founder_time: 3-4 hours/day for data and coordination, with survey, testing, and removal performed by specialists
economics.gross_margin_basis: Target 35-55% after site survey, testing, deconstruction coordination, storage exceptions, and sales support
economics.payback: Unvalidated: four medium projects with 20000 PLN contribution each could repay the pilot in 18-24 months
economics.pricing: Unvalidated: 5000-25000 PLN project-management fee plus 10-18% commission on recovered material value
economics.retention_or_repeat: Projects are episodic; property portfolios and demolition partners can supply repeat inventory

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Exclusive future inventory, realized-price data, buyer specifications, and reliable deconstruction partners
fingerprint.customer: Property owners, demolition contractors, fit-out firms, and contractors buying reusable fixtures or materials
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Warsaw property managers and demolition firms first, then contractor buyers and insurer-approved categories
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Pre-demolition audit, exclusive catalog, evidence file, reservation, deconstruction coordination, and payment
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Exchange earns seller management fee and buyer commission when a reserved lot is collected
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A renovation or demolition creates a deadline to remove valuable components before they become mixed waste

founder_fit: Inventory matching and pricing suit analytical automation
Warsaw offers a dense starting geography
Field and deconstruction work can be delegated
The founder can validate categories before carrying inventory
risks: Hazardous materials, hidden damage, and product liability are material
Project schedules can make matching and collection impractical
Storage and transport can overwhelm commission economics

structure.commercial_archetype: Exclusive inventory brokerage with deconstruction-management fees
structure.control_point: Contractual pre-demolition salvage rights and a verified inventory reserved before material removal
structure.critical_dependency: Owners must grant early access and buyers must accept the safety, performance, timing, and logistics of reused materials

thesis: Secure exclusive, time-bound salvage rights before commercial renovations or demolitions, inventory reusable fixtures and selected construction products, attach available performance evidence, and pre-sell lots to contractors before removal. The defensible position is control of supply before demolition plus buyer demand data, not a public classifieds site.
title: Pre-Demolition Material Rights Exchange
uncertainties: Which product categories can be lawfully and economically reused
Owner willingness to grant exclusive salvage rights early
Buyer acceptance of evidence for previously installed products
